questions.text: Let $f(x)=\dfrac{2^{x+2}+16}{2^{2x+1}+2^{x+4}+32}$. Then the value of $8\left(f\left(\dfrac{1}{15}\right)+f\left(\dfrac{2}{15}\right)+\ldots+f\left(\dfrac{59}{15}\right)\right)$ is equal to
questions.sol:
Put $t=2^x$: $f(x)=\dfrac{4(t+4)}{2(t+4)^2}=\dfrac{2}{t+4}$.
For $4-x$, $2^{4-x}=\dfrac{16}{t}$, so $f(4-x)=\dfrac{2t}{16+4t}=\dfrac{t}{2(t+4)}$. Hence $f(x)+f(4-x)=\dfrac12$.
The arguments $\dfrac{k}{15}$ and $\dfrac{60-k}{15}$ add to 4, giving 29 pairs ($k=1,\ldots,29$) and the middle term $f(2)=\dfrac{2}{8}=\dfrac14$.
Sum $=\dfrac{29}{2}+\dfrac14=\dfrac{59}{4}$, and $8\times\dfrac{59}{4}=118$.

questions.text: The product of all the rational roots of the equation $(x^2-9x+11)^2-(x-4)(x-5)=3$, is equal to
questions.sol:
Let $y=x^2-9x$. Then $(x-4)(x-5)=y+20$ and the equation becomes $(y+11)^2-(y+20)-3=0$, i.e. $y^2+21y+98=0$, so $y=-7$ or $y=-14$.
$x^2-9x+7=0$ has discriminant $53$, so its roots are irrational.
$x^2-9x+14=0$ gives $x=2,7$.
Product of the rational roots $=14$.

questions.text: If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the roots of the equation $2z^2-3z-2i=0$, where $i=\sqrt{-1}$, then $16\cdot\operatorname{Re}\left(\dfrac{\alpha^{19}+\beta^{19}+\alpha^{11}+\beta^{11}}{\alpha^{15}+\beta^{15}}\right)\cdot\operatorname{Im}\left(\dfrac{\alpha^{19}+\beta^{19}+\alpha^{11}+\beta^{11}}{\alpha^{15}+\beta^{15}}\right)$ is equal to
questions.sol:
$\alpha+\beta=\dfrac32$, $\alpha\beta=-i$, so $(\alpha\beta)^4=1$.
$(\alpha^{15}+\beta^{15})(\alpha^4+\beta^4)=\alpha^{19}+\beta^{19}+(\alpha\beta)^4(\alpha^{11}+\beta^{11})=\alpha^{19}+\beta^{19}+\alpha^{11}+\beta^{11}$.
So the ratio equals $\alpha^4+\beta^4$.
$\alpha^2+\beta^2=\dfrac94+2i$, $\alpha^4+\beta^4=\left(\dfrac94+2i\right)^2-2(\alpha\beta)^2=\dfrac{81}{16}-4+9i+2=\dfrac{49}{16}+9i$.
$16\times\dfrac{49}{16}\times9=441$.

questions.text:
If the system of equations
$2x-y+z=4$
$5x+\lambda y+3z=12$
$100x-47y+\mu z=212$,
has infinitely many solutions, then $\mu-2\lambda$ is equal to
questions.sol:
For infinitely many solutions the third equation must be a combination $a(\text{first})+b(\text{second})$.
$x$: $2a+5b=100$; constants: $4a+12b=212 \Rightarrow a+3b=53$. So $b=6$, $a=35$.
$y$: $-a+\lambda b=-47 \Rightarrow 6\lambda=-12 \Rightarrow \lambda=-2$.
$z$: $\mu=a+3b=53$.
$\mu-2\lambda=53+4=57$.

questions.text: Let $S_n=\dfrac12+\dfrac16+\dfrac1{12}+\dfrac1{20}+\ldots$ upto $n$ terms. If the sum of the first six terms of an A.P. with first term $-p$ and common difference $p$ is $\sqrt{2026S_{2025}}$, then the absolute difference betwen $20^{\text{th}}$ and $15^{\text{th}}$ terms of the A.P. is
questions.sol:
$\dfrac{1}{k(k+1)}=\dfrac1k-\dfrac1{k+1}$, so $S_n=\dfrac{n}{n+1}$ and $\sqrt{2026S_{2025}}=\sqrt{2025}=45$.
Sum of six terms $=\dfrac62\left(-2p+5p\right)=9p=45 \Rightarrow p=5$.
$|a_{20}-a_{15}|=5p=25$.

questions.text: For some $n\neq10$, let the coefficients of the 5th, 6th and 7th terms in the binomial expansion of $(1+x)^{n+4}$ be in A.P. Then the largest coefficient in the expansion of $(1+x)^{n+4}$ is:
questions.sol:
Let $m=n+4$. $2\binom{m}{5}=\binom{m}{4}+\binom{m}{6}$. Dividing by $\binom{m}{4}$: $\dfrac{2(m-4)}{5}=1+\dfrac{(m-4)(m-5)}{30}$, which simplifies to $m^2-21m+98=0$, so $m=7$ or $14$.
$n\neq10$ rules out $m=14$, so $m=7$.
Largest coefficient in $(1+x)^7$ is $\binom73=35$.

questions.text: For a statistical data $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_{10}$ of 10 values, a student obtained the mean as 5.5 and $\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{10}x_i^2=371$. He later found that he had noted two values in the data incorrectly as 4 and 5, instead of the correct values 6 and 8, respectively. The variance of the corrected data is
questions.sol:
Original sum $=55$. Corrected sum $=55-4-5+6+8=60$, so the mean is $6$.
Corrected $\sum x_i^2=371-16-25+36+64=430$.
Variance $=\dfrac{430}{10}-6^2=43-36=7$.

questions.text: A and B alternately throw a pair of dice. A wins if he throws a sum of 5 before B throws a sum of 8, and B wins if he throws a sum of 8 before A throws a sum of 5. The probability, that A wins if A makes the first throw, is
questions.sol:
$P(\text{sum }5)=\dfrac{4}{36}=\dfrac19$, $P(\text{sum }8)=\dfrac{5}{36}$.
One full round with no winner has probability $\dfrac89\cdot\dfrac{31}{36}=\dfrac{62}{81}$.
$P(A)=\dfrac{1/9}{1-62/81}=\dfrac{1/9}{19/81}=\dfrac{9}{19}$.

questions.text: Let the lines $3x-4y-\alpha=0$, $8x-11y-33=0$, and $2x-3y+\lambda=0$ be concurrent. If the image of the point $(1, 2)$ in the line $2x-3y+\lambda=0$ is $\left(\dfrac{57}{13}, \dfrac{-40}{13}\right)$, then $|\alpha\lambda|$ is equal to
questions.sol:
The midpoint of $(1,2)$ and its image, $\left(\dfrac{35}{13},-\dfrac{7}{13}\right)$, lies on the line: $\dfrac{70}{13}+\dfrac{21}{13}+\lambda=0 \Rightarrow \lambda=-7$.
$2x-3y=7$ and $8x-11y=33$ meet at $(11,5)$.
Concurrency: $33-20-\alpha=0 \Rightarrow \alpha=13$.
$|\alpha\lambda|=91$.

questions.text: Let circle C be the image of $x^2+y^2-2x+4y-4=0$ in the line $2x-3y+5=0$ and A be the point on C such that OA is parallel to x-axis and A lies on the right hand side of the centre O of C. If $B(\alpha, \beta)$, with $\beta<4$, lies on C such that the length of the arc AB is $(1/6)^{\text{th}}$ of the perimeter of C, then $\beta-\sqrt3\alpha$ is equal to
questions.sol:
The given circle has centre $(1,-2)$ and radius 3. Reflecting the centre in $2x-3y+5=0$ (value $2+6+5=13$): $(1,-2)-\dfrac{2\cdot13}{13}(2,-3)=(-3,4)$.
So O $=(-3,4)$, radius 3, and A $=(0,4)$.
Arc AB is $\dfrac16$ of the circumference, so $\angle AOB=60^\circ$; with $\beta<4$, B $=\left(-3+3\cos60^\circ,\ 4-3\sin60^\circ\right)=\left(-\dfrac32,\ 4-\dfrac{3\sqrt3}{2}\right)$.
$\beta-\sqrt3\alpha=4-\dfrac{3\sqrt3}{2}+\dfrac{3\sqrt3}{2}=4$.

questions.text: Let the product of the focal distances of the point $\left(\sqrt3, \dfrac12\right)$ on the ellipse $\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1$, $(a>b)$, be $\dfrac74$. Then the absolute difference of the eccentricities of two such ellipses is
questions.sol:
Focal distances are $a\pm ex$, so $a^2-e^2x^2=a^2-3e^2=\dfrac74$. With $e^2=1-\dfrac{b^2}{a^2}$ and $A=a^2$: $A-3+\dfrac{3b^2}{A}=\dfrac74$.
The point lies on the ellipse: $\dfrac3A+\dfrac1{4b^2}=1 \Rightarrow b^2=\dfrac{A}{4(A-3)}$.
Substituting: $A-\dfrac{19}{4}+\dfrac{3}{4(A-3)}=0 \Rightarrow 4A^2-31A+60=0 \Rightarrow A=4$ or $\dfrac{15}{4}$.
$A=4$: $b^2=1$, $e^2=\dfrac34$. $A=\dfrac{15}{4}$: $b^2=\dfrac54$, $e^2=\dfrac23$.
Difference $=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}-\dfrac{\sqrt2}{\sqrt3}=\dfrac{3-2\sqrt2}{2\sqrt3}$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0}\operatorname{cosec}x\left(\sqrt{2\cos^2x+3\cos x}-\sqrt{\cos^2x+\sin x+4}\right)$ is:
questions.sol:
Both roots tend to $\sqrt5$, so the bracket $g(x)\to0$ and $\operatorname{cosec}x\sim\dfrac1x$; the limit is $g'(0)$.
$\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(2\cos^2x+3\cos x\right)=-4\cos x\sin x-3\sin x\to0$; $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\cos^2x+\sin x+4\right)=-2\cos x\sin x+\cos x\to1$.
$g'(0)=\dfrac{0}{2\sqrt5}-\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt5}=-\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt5}$.

questions.text: Let $\vec a=\hat i+2\hat j+3\hat k$, $\vec b=3\hat i+\hat j-\hat k$ and $\vec c$ be three vectors such that $\vec c$ is coplanar with $\vec a$ and $\vec b$. If the vector $\vec c$ is perpendicular to $\vec b$ and $\vec a\cdot\vec c=5$, then $|\vec c|$ is equal to
questions.sol:
Let $\vec c=x\vec a+y\vec b$. $\vec a\cdot\vec b=2$, $|\vec a|^2=14$, $|\vec b|^2=11$.
$\vec c\cdot\vec b=0$: $2x+11y=0$. $\vec a\cdot\vec c=5$: $14x+2y=5$.
So $x=\dfrac{11}{30}$, $y=-\dfrac1{15}$ and $\vec c=\dfrac16(\hat i+4\hat j+7\hat k)$.
$|\vec c|=\dfrac{\sqrt{66}}{6}=\sqrt{\dfrac{11}{6}}$.

questions.text: Let in a $\Delta ABC$, the length of the side AC be 6, the vertex B be $(1, 2, 3)$ and the vertices A, C lie on the line $\dfrac{x-6}{3}=\dfrac{y-7}{2}=\dfrac{z-7}{-2}$. Then the area (in sq. units) of $\Delta ABC$ is:
questions.sol:
The height is the distance of B from the line through $(6,7,7)$ with direction $(3,2,-2)$.
Vector to B: $(5,5,4)$, length$^2=66$; its component along the line is $\dfrac{15+10-8}{\sqrt{17}}=\sqrt{17}$.
Distance $=\sqrt{66-17}=7$.
Area $=\dfrac12\times6\times7=21$.

questions.text: Let $f:\mathbb{R}-\{0\}\to\mathbb{R}$ be a function such that $f(x)-6f\left(\dfrac1x\right)=\dfrac{35}{3x}-\dfrac52$. If the $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0}\left(\dfrac{1}{\alpha x}+f(x)\right)=\beta$; $\alpha, \beta\in\mathbb{R}$, then $\alpha+2\beta$ is equal to
questions.sol:
Replace $x$ by $\dfrac1x$: $f\left(\dfrac1x\right)-6f(x)=\dfrac{35x}{3}-\dfrac52$.
Eliminating $f\left(\dfrac1x\right)$: $f(x)=36f(x)+70x-15+\dfrac{35}{3x}-\dfrac52$, so $f(x)=-2x-\dfrac{1}{3x}+\dfrac12$.
$\dfrac{1}{\alpha x}+f(x)=\left(\dfrac1\alpha-\dfrac13\right)\dfrac1x-2x+\dfrac12$ has a finite limit only if $\alpha=3$; then $\beta=\dfrac12$.
$\alpha+2\beta=4$.

questions.text:
Consider the region $R=\left\{(x,y): x\le y\le9-\dfrac{11}{3}x^2, x\ge0\right\}$.
The area, of the largest rectangle of sides parallel to the coordinate axes and inscribed in R, is:
questions.sol:
Take the rectangle $0\le x\le t$, $t\le y\le9-\dfrac{11}{3}t^2$ (its lower-right corner on $y=x$, upper-right corner on the parabola).
Area $A(t)=t\left(9-t-\dfrac{11}{3}t^2\right)$. $A'(t)=9-2t-11t^2=0 \Rightarrow t=\dfrac{9}{11}$.
$A=\dfrac{9}{11}\left(9-\dfrac{9}{11}-\dfrac{27}{11}\right)=\dfrac{9}{11}\cdot\dfrac{63}{11}=\dfrac{567}{121}$.

questions.text: The area of the region $\{(x, y) : x^2+4x+2\le y\le|x+2|\}$ is equal to
questions.sol:
Put $u=x+2$: $u^2-2\le y\le|u|$. This needs $u^2-|u|-2\le0$, i.e. $|u|\le2$.
By symmetry, area $=2\displaystyle\int_0^2\left(u-u^2+2\right)du=2\left(2-\dfrac83+4\right)=\dfrac{20}{3}$.

questions.text: Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation $\left(xy-5x^2\sqrt{1+x^2}\right)dx+(1+x^2)dy=0$, $y(0)=0$. Then $y(\sqrt3)$ is equal to
questions.sol:
$\dfrac{dy}{dx}+\dfrac{x}{1+x^2}y=\dfrac{5x^2}{\sqrt{1+x^2}}$. Integrating factor $\sqrt{1+x^2}$.
$\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(y\sqrt{1+x^2}\right)=5x^2 \Rightarrow y\sqrt{1+x^2}=\dfrac{5x^3}{3}+C$, and $y(0)=0$ gives $C=0$.
$x=\sqrt3$: $2y=5\sqrt3$, so $y=\dfrac{5\sqrt3}{2}$.

questions.text: Let $S=\{p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_{10}\}$ be the set of first ten prime numbers. Let $A=S\cup P$, where P is the set of all possible products of distinct elements of S. Then the number of all ordered pairs $(x, y)$, $x\in S$, $y\in A$, such that $x$ divides $y$, is _____.
questions.sol:
A consists of the products of the primes in every non-empty subset of S (single primes included).
For a fixed prime $x$, $x\mid y$ exactly when the subset for $y$ contains $x$: $2^9=512$ choices.
Total $=10\times512=5120$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let A be a $3\times3$ matrix such that $X^TAX=O$ for all nonzero $3\times1$ matrices $X=\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{bmatrix}$. If $A\begin{bmatrix}1\\1\\1\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}1\\4\\-5\end{bmatrix}$, $A\begin{bmatrix}1\\2\\1\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}0\\4\\-8\end{bmatrix}$, and $\det(\operatorname{adj}(2(A+I)))=2^\alpha3^\beta5^\gamma$, $\alpha, \beta, \gamma\in\mathbb{N}$, then $\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2$ is _____.
questions.sol:
$X^TAX=0$ for all $X$ means A is skew-symmetric: $A=\begin{bmatrix}0&a&b\\-a&0&c\\-b&-c&0\end{bmatrix}$.
From the data: $a+b=1$, $c-a=4$, $2a+b=0$, so $a=-1$, $b=2$, $c=3$ (the remaining equations check).
For a skew-symmetric $3\times3$ matrix, $\det(I+A)=1+a^2+b^2+c^2=15$.
$\det(\operatorname{adj}M)=(\det M)^2$ for $3\times3$: $(2^3\cdot15)^2=120^2=2^6\,3^2\,5^2$.
$36+4+4=44$.

questions.text: The number of 3-digit numbers, that are divisible by 2 and 3, but not divisible by 4 and 9, is _____.
questions.note: NTA final key gives 125, which reads "not divisible by 4 and 9" as "not divisible by both 4 and 9" (that is, not by 36). Read as "divisible by neither 4 nor 9", the count would be $150-75-50+25=50$.
questions.sol:
Divisible by 2 and 3 means divisible by 6: $102,\ldots,996$, that is $150$ numbers.
Divisible by both 4 and 9 means divisible by 36: $108,\ldots,972$, that is $25$ numbers.
$150-25=125$.

questions.text: If for some $\alpha, \beta$; $\alpha\le\beta$, $\alpha+\beta=8$ and $\sec^2(\tan^{-1}\alpha)+\operatorname{cosec}^2(\cot^{-1}\beta)=36$, then $\alpha^2+\beta$ is _____.
questions.sol:
$\sec^2(\tan^{-1}\alpha)=1+\alpha^2$ and $\operatorname{cosec}^2(\cot^{-1}\beta)=1+\beta^2$, so $\alpha^2+\beta^2=34$.
With $\alpha+\beta=8$: $\alpha\beta=15$, so $\alpha=3$, $\beta=5$.
$\alpha^2+\beta=14$.

questions.text: For an experimental expression $y=\dfrac{32.3\times1125}{27.4}$, where all the digits are significant. Then to report the value of $y$ we should write
questions.sol:
$\dfrac{32.3\times1125}{27.4}=1326.19\ldots$
In multiplication and division the result keeps as many significant figures as the least precise factor: 32.3 and 27.4 have 3.
So $y=1330$ (3 significant figures).

questions.text: An object of mass 'm' is projected from origin in a vertical xy plane at an angle $45^\circ$ with the x-axis with an initial velocity $v_0$. The magnitude and direction of the angular momentum of the object with respect to origin, when it reaches at the maximum height, will be [g is acceleration due to gravity]
questions.sol:
At the top the velocity is $\dfrac{v_0}{\sqrt2}\hat i$ and the height is $H=\dfrac{v_0^2\sin^245^\circ}{2g}=\dfrac{v_0^2}{4g}$.
$\vec L=m\,\vec r\times\vec v$; only $y=H$ contributes: $\vec L=m\left(H\hat j\right)\times\left(\dfrac{v_0}{\sqrt2}\hat i\right)=-\dfrac{mHv_0}{\sqrt2}\hat k$.
$|\vec L|=\dfrac{mv_0^3}{4\sqrt2g}$, along the negative z-axis.

questions.text: A car of mass 'm' moves on a banked road having radius 'r' and banking angle $\theta$. To avoid slipping from banked road, the maximum permissible speed of the car is $v_0$. The coefficient of friction $\mu$ between the wheels of the car and the banked road is
questions.sol:
At the maximum speed, friction acts down the slope: $v_0^2=rg\,\dfrac{\tan\theta+\mu}{1-\mu\tan\theta}$.
$v_0^2-\mu v_0^2\tan\theta=rg\tan\theta+\mu rg \Rightarrow \mu=\dfrac{v_0^2-rg\tan\theta}{rg+v_0^2\tan\theta}$.

questions.text: A force $F=\alpha+\beta x^2$ acts on an object in the x-direction. The work done by the force is 5 J when the object is displaced by 1 m. If the constant $\alpha=1$N then $\beta$ will be
questions.sol:
$W=\displaystyle\int_0^1(\alpha+\beta x^2)\,dx=\alpha+\dfrac{\beta}{3}=5$.
With $\alpha=1$: $\beta=12$ N/m$^2$.

questions.text: A uniform solid cylinder of mass 'm' and radius 'r' rolls along an inclined rough plane of inclination $45^\circ$. If it starts to roll from rest from the top of the plane then the linear acceleration of the cylinder's axis will be
questions.sol:
For rolling without slipping, $a=\dfrac{g\sin\theta}{1+I/mr^2}$; for a solid cylinder $I/mr^2=\dfrac12$.
$a=\dfrac23g\sin45^\circ=\dfrac{2g}{3\sqrt2}=\dfrac{\sqrt2g}{3}$.

questions.text: A satellite is launched into a circular orbit of radius 'R' around the earth. A second satellite is launched into an orbit of radius 1.03 R. The time period of revolution of the second satellite is larger than the first one approximately by
questions.sol: Kepler's third law: $T\propto R^{3/2}$, so $\dfrac{\Delta T}{T}\approx\dfrac32\cdot\dfrac{\Delta R}{R}=\dfrac32\times3\%=4.5\%$.

questions.text: The amount of work done to break a big water drop of radius 'R' into 27 small drops of equal radius is 10 J. The work done required to break the same big drop into 64 small drops of equal radius will be
questions.sol:
Volume is conserved, so $n$ drops have radius $r=Rn^{-1/3}$ and total area $4\pi R^2n^{1/3}$.
$W=4\pi R^2T\left(n^{1/3}-1\right)$: for $n=27$ the factor is 2, for $n=64$ it is 3.
$W=10\times\dfrac32=15$ J.

questions.text:
An ideal gas goes from an initial state to final state. During the process, the pressure of gas increases linearly with temperature.
A. The work done by gas during the process is zero.
B. The heat added to gas is different from change in its internal energy.
C. The volume of the gas is increased.
D. The internal energy of the gas is increased.
E. The process is isochoric (constant volume process)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
$p\propto T$ for an ideal gas means $V=\dfrac{nRT}{p}$ is constant: the process is isochoric (E).
So $W=0$ (A), $Q=\Delta U$ (B false) and the volume does not change (C false).
Since $p$ increases, $T$ increases and so does the internal energy (D).
Correct: A, D, E.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A particle is executing simple harmonic motion with time period 2 s and amplitude 1 cm. If D and d are the total distance and displacement covered by the particle in 12.5 s, then $\dfrac{D}{d}$ is
questions.sol:
$12.5$ s $=6T+\dfrac{T}{4}$. Six full periods give a distance of $6\times4A=24$ cm and no displacement.
Starting from the mean position (or from an extreme), the extra quarter period covers $A=1$ cm, with displacement of magnitude 1 cm.
$\dfrac{D}{d}=\dfrac{25}{1}=25$.

questions.text: An alternating current is given by $I=I_A\sin\omega t+I_B\cos\omega t$. The r.m.s current will be
questions.sol:
$I=I_0\sin(\omega t+\phi)$ with $I_0=\sqrt{I_A^2+I_B^2}$.
$I_{rms}=\dfrac{I_0}{\sqrt2}=\sqrt{\dfrac{I_A^2+I_B^2}{2}}$.

questions.text:
A parallel plate capacitor was made with two rectangular plates, each with a length of $l=3$ cm and breath of $b=1$ cm. The distance between the plates is 3 $\mu$m. Out of the following, which are the ways to increase the capacitance by a factor of 10?
A. $l=30$ cm, $b=1$ cm, $d=1$ $\mu$m
B. $l=3$ cm, $b=1$ cm, $d=30$ $\mu$m
C. $l=6$ cm, $b=5$ cm, $d=3$ $\mu$m
D. $l=1$ cm, $b=1$ cm, $d=10$ $\mu$m
E. $l=5$ cm, $b=2$ cm, $d=1$ $\mu$m
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
$C=\dfrac{\varepsilon_0lb}{d}\propto\dfrac{lb}{d}$. Original: $\dfrac{3\times1}{3}=1$ (cm$^2$/$\mu$m).
A: 30; B: 0.1; C: $\dfrac{30}{3}=10$; D: 0.1; E: $\dfrac{10}{1}=10$.
C and E increase the capacitance tenfold.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Consider a parallel plate capacitor of area A (of each plate) and separation 'd' between the plates. If E is the electric field and $\varepsilon_0$ is the permittivity of free space between the plates, then potential energy stored in the capacitor is
questions.sol:
Energy density $=\dfrac12\varepsilon_0E^2$, and the field fills the volume $Ad$.
$U=\dfrac12\varepsilon_0E^2Ad$.

questions.text: The Young's double slit interference experiment is performed using light consisting of 480 nm and 600 nm wavelengths to form interference patterns. The least number of the bright fringes of 480 nm light that are required for the first coincidence with the bright fringes formed by 600 nm light is
questions.sol:
Bright fringes coincide when $n_1(480)=n_2(600)$, i.e. $4n_1=5n_2$.
The smallest solution is $n_1=5$, $n_2=4$: the 5th bright fringe of 480 nm light falls on the 4th of 600 nm light.
So 5 bright fringes of 480 nm light are needed.

questions.text: A thin plano convex lens made of glass of refractive index 1.5 is immersed in a liquid of refractive index 1.2. When the plane side of the lens is silver coated for complete reflection, the lens immersed in the liquid behaves like a concave mirror of focal length 0.2 m. The radius of curvature of the curved surface of the lens is
questions.sol:
In the liquid, $\dfrac1{f_L}=\left(\dfrac{1.5}{1.2}-1\right)\dfrac1R=\dfrac{1}{4R}$, so $f_L=4R$.
Light passes through the lens twice and the plane mirror adds no power: $P=\dfrac{2}{f_L}$, so the equivalent mirror has focal length $\dfrac{f_L}{2}=2R$.
$2R=0.2$ m $\Rightarrow R=0.10$ m.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: What is the relative decrease in focal length of a lens for an increase in optical power by 0.1D from 2.5D ? ['D' stands for dioptre]
questions.sol: $f=\dfrac1P$, so $\dfrac{|\Delta f|}{f}=\dfrac{\Delta P}{P}=\dfrac{0.1}{2.5}=0.04$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A plano-convex lens having radius of curvature of first surface 2 cm exhibits focal length of $f_1$ in air. Another plano-convex lens with first surface radius of curvature 3 cm has focal length of $f_2$ when it is immersed in a liquid of refractive index 1.2. If both the lenses are made of same glass of refractive index 1.5, the ratio of $f_1$ and $f_2$ will be
questions.sol:
$\dfrac1{f_1}=(1.5-1)\dfrac12 \Rightarrow f_1=4$ cm.
$\dfrac1{f_2}=\left(\dfrac{1.5}{1.2}-1\right)\dfrac13=\dfrac1{12} \Rightarrow f_2=12$ cm.
$f_1:f_2=1:3$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: An electron of mass 'm' with an initial velocity $\vec v=v_0\hat i\ (v_0>0)$ enters an electric field $\vec E=-E_0\hat k$. If the initial de Broglie wavelength is $\lambda_0$, the value after time t would be
questions.sol:
The force on the electron is $-e\vec E=eE_0\hat k$, perpendicular to $\vec v_0$, so it gains $v_z=\dfrac{eE_0t}{m}$ while $v_x=v_0$ is unchanged.
$p=mv_0\sqrt{1+\dfrac{e^2E_0^2t^2}{m^2v_0^2}}$ and $\lambda=\dfrac hp$, so $\lambda=\dfrac{\lambda_0}{\sqrt{1+\dfrac{e^2E_0^2t^2}{m^2v_0^2}}}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.text: During the transition of electron from state A to state C of a Bohr atom, the wavelength of emitted radiation is 2000 $\mathrm{\mathring{A}}$ and it becomes 6000 $\mathrm{\mathring{A}}$ when the electron jumps from state B to state C. Then the wavelength of the radiation emitted during the transition of electrons from state A to state B is
questions.sol:
Energies add: $E_{AC}=E_{AB}+E_{BC}$, so $\dfrac1{\lambda_{AB}}=\dfrac1{2000}-\dfrac1{6000}=\dfrac{1}{3000}$.
$\lambda_{AB}=3000$ $\mathrm{\mathring{A}}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Consider the following statements:
A. The junction area of solar cell is made very narrow compared to a photo diode.
B. Solar cells are not connected with any external bias.
C. LED is made of lightly doped p-n junction.
D. Increase of forward current results in continuous increase of LED light intensity.
E. LEDs have to be connected in forward bias for emission of light.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
A: false; a solar cell has a large junction area to collect more light.
B: true; a solar cell generates its own emf and needs no bias.
C: false; an LED is heavily doped.
D: false; the intensity rises with forward current up to a maximum and then falls.
E: true; an LED emits light only when forward biased.
Correct: B, E.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The least count of a screw guage is 0.01 mm. If the pitch is increased by 75% and number of divisions on the circular scale is reduced by 50%, the new least count will be _____ $\times10^{-3}$ mm
questions.sol:
Least count $=\dfrac{\text{pitch}}{N}$.
New least count $=\dfrac{1.75p}{0.5N}=3.5\times0.01=0.035$ mm $=35\times10^{-3}$ mm.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The temperature of 1 mole of an ideal monoatomic gas is increased by $50^\circ$C at constant pressure. The total heat added and change in internal energy are $E_1$ and $E_2$, respectively. If $\dfrac{E_1}{E_2}=\dfrac{x}{9}$ then the value of $x$ is _____
questions.sol:
$E_1=nC_p\Delta T$ and $E_2=nC_v\Delta T$, so $\dfrac{E_1}{E_2}=\dfrac{C_p}{C_v}=\dfrac53$ for a monoatomic gas.
$\dfrac53=\dfrac{x}{9} \Rightarrow x=15$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A wire of resistance 9 $\Omega$ is bent to form an equilateral triangle. Then the equivalent resistance across any two vertices will be _____ohm.
questions.sol:
Each side is $3\ \Omega$. Between two vertices, one side ($3\ \Omega$) is in parallel with the other two in series ($6\ \Omega$).
$R=\dfrac{3\times6}{9}=2\ \Omega$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
A current of 5A exists in a square loop of side $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}$ m. Then the magnitude of the magnetic field B at the centre of the square loop will be $p\times10^{-6}$ T. where, value of $p$ is _____.
[Take $\mu_0=4\pi\times10^{-7}$ T m A$^{-1}$].
questions.sol:
Each side is at distance $\dfrac a2$ from the centre and subtends $45^\circ$ on each side: $B_1=\dfrac{\mu_0I}{4\pi(a/2)}\left(2\sin45^\circ\right)$.
Total $B=4B_1=\dfrac{2\sqrt2\,\mu_0I}{\pi a}=\dfrac{2\sqrt2\times4\pi\times10^{-7}\times5}{\pi/\sqrt2}=80\times10^{-7}$ T.
$B=8\times10^{-6}$ T, so $p=8$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A square loop of sides $a=1$ m is held normally in front of a point charge $q=1$C. The flux of the electric field through the shaded region is $\dfrac5p\times\dfrac{1}{\varepsilon_0}\dfrac{\mathrm{Nm^2}}{\mathrm{C}}$, where the value of $p$ is _____.
questions.note: The text does not state the distance of the charge from the loop; NTA's answer (48) corresponds to the charge being at distance $a/2$ from the centre of the loop, so that the loop is one face of a cube centred on the charge.
questions.sol:
With the charge on the axis at distance $\dfrac a2$ from the centre of the loop, the loop is one face of a cube of side $a$ centred on the charge, so the whole loop receives $\dfrac{q}{6\varepsilon_0}$, i.e. $\dfrac{q}{24\varepsilon_0}$ per quarter.
The shaded region is two full quarters plus half of a third quarter (the triangle cut off by the diagonal), i.e. $2.5$ quarters.
Flux $=\dfrac{2.5}{24}\cdot\dfrac{1}{\varepsilon_0}=\dfrac{5}{48}\cdot\dfrac1{\varepsilon_0}$, so $p=48$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Which of the following linear combination of atomic orbitals will lead to formation of molecular orbitals in homonuclear diatomic molecules [internuclear axis in z- direction] ?
A. $2p_z$ and $2p_x$
B. $2s$ and $2p_x$
C. $3d_{xy}$ and $3d_{x^2-y^2}$
D. $2s$ and $2p_z$
E. $2p_z$ and $3d_{x^2-y^2}$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
Atomic orbitals combine only if they have the same symmetry about the internuclear (z) axis, giving non-zero net overlap.
$2s$ and $2p_z$ are both symmetric about z and overlap along the axis (D).
$2p_z$/$2p_x$, $2s$/$2p_x$, $3d_{xy}$/$3d_{x^2-y^2}$ and $2p_z$/$3d_{x^2-y^2}$ all have zero net overlap.
D only.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Which of the following statement is true with respect to $\mathrm{H_2O}$, $\mathrm{NH_3}$ and $\mathrm{CH_4}$ ?
A. The central atoms of all the molecules are $sp^3$ hybridized.
B. The H-O-H, H-N-H and H-C-H angles in the above molecules are $104.5^\circ$, $107.5^\circ$ and $109.5^\circ$, respectively.
C. The increasing order of dipole moment is $\mathrm{CH_4}<\mathrm{NH_3}<\mathrm{H_2O}$ .
D. Both $\mathrm{H_2O}$ and $\mathrm{NH_3}$ are Lewis acids and $\mathrm{CH_4}$ is a Lewis base.
E. A solution of $\mathrm{NH_3}$ in $\mathrm{H_2O}$ is basic. In this solution $\mathrm{NH_3}$ and $\mathrm{H_2O}$ act as Lowry-Bronsted acid and base respectively.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A, B, C and E Only
questions.sol:
A: true; O, N and C are all $sp^3$ hybridised.
B: true; lone pairs squeeze the angles from $109.5^\circ$ (CH$_4$) to about $107^\circ$ (NH$_3$) and $104.5^\circ$ (H$_2$O).
C: true; CH$_4$ is non-polar and H$_2$O (1.85 D) is more polar than NH$_3$ (1.47 D).
D: false; H$_2$O and NH$_3$ are lone-pair donors (Lewis bases) and CH$_4$ is neither.
E: false; NH$_3$ accepts a proton (base) and H$_2$O donates it (acid).
Correct: A, B and C.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Let us consider an endothermic reaction which is non-spontaneous at the freezing point of water. However, the reaction is spontaneous at boiling point of water. Choose the correct option.
questions.sol:
Endothermic means $\Delta H>0$. $\Delta G=\Delta H-T\Delta S$ is positive at 273 K but negative at 373 K, so $\Delta G$ falls as $T$ rises, which needs $\Delta S>0$.
Both $\Delta H$ and $\Delta S$ are positive.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Consider the given plots of vapour pressure (VP) vs temperature(T/K). Which amongst the following options is correct graphical representation showing $\Delta T_f$, depression in the freezing point of a solvent in a solution?
questions.sol:
A solute lowers the vapour pressure, so the solution curve lies below the liquid-solvent curve at every temperature.
The freezing point is where the vapour pressure of the liquid equals that of the solid solvent. The steep solid curve meets the liquid-solvent curve at $T_f^\circ$ and the lower solution curve at a lower temperature $T_f$.
Graph (4) shows exactly this, with $\Delta T_f=T_f^\circ-T_f$.
Graph (1) puts the solution curve above the liquid solvent; graphs (2) and (3) read two temperatures at one vapour pressure with no solid-liquid crossing, which is not how a freezing point is found.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: $K_{sp}$ for $\mathrm{Cr(OH)_3}$ is $1.6\times10^{-30}$. What is the molar solubility of this salt in water?
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{Cr(OH)_3\rightleftharpoons Cr^{3+}+3OH^-}$: $K_{sp}=s(3s)^3=27s^4$.
$s=\sqrt[4]{\dfrac{1.6\times10^{-30}}{27}}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
For the given cell
$\mathrm{Fe^{2+}(aq)+Ag^+(aq)\rightarrow Fe^{3+}(aq)+Ag(s)}$
The standard cell potential of the above reaction is
Given:
$\mathrm{Ag^++e^-\rightarrow Ag}$ $\quad E^\ominus=x$ V
$\mathrm{Fe^{2+}+2e^-\rightarrow Fe}$ $\quad E^\ominus=y$ V
$\mathrm{Fe^{3+}+3e^-\rightarrow Fe}$ $\quad E^\ominus=z$ V
questions.sol:
Combine through $\Delta G^\ominus=-nFE^\ominus$: $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}+e^-\rightarrow Fe^{2+}}$ is $(\mathrm{Fe^{3+}\to Fe})-(\mathrm{Fe^{2+}\to Fe})$, so $E^\ominus_{\mathrm{Fe^{3+}/Fe^{2+}}}=3z-2y$.
$E^\ominus_{cell}=E^\ominus_{\mathrm{Ag^+/Ag}}-E^\ominus_{\mathrm{Fe^{3+}/Fe^{2+}}}=x-(3z-2y)=x+2y-3z$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: For a reaction, $\mathrm{N_2O_5(g)\rightarrow2NO_2(g)+\dfrac12O_2(g)}$ in a constant volume container, no products were present initially. The final pressure of the system when 50% of reaction gets completed is
questions.sol:
Start with $p_0$ of $\mathrm{N_2O_5}$. At 50% conversion: $\mathrm{N_2O_5}$ $\dfrac{p_0}{2}$, $\mathrm{NO_2}$ $p_0$, $\mathrm{O_2}$ $\dfrac{p_0}{4}$.
Total $=\dfrac{7}{4}p_0$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Which of the following statements are NOT true about the periodic table?
A. The properties of elements are function of atomic weights.
B. The properties of elements are function of atomic numbers.
C. Elements having similar outer electronic configurations are arranged in same period.
D. An element's location reflects the quantum numbers of the last filled orbital.
E. The number of elements in a period is same as the number of atomic orbitals available in energy level that is being filled.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
A is not true: the modern periodic law uses atomic numbers (B is true).
C is not true: similar outer configurations put elements in the same group, not period.
D is true.
E is not true: a period holds twice as many elements as the orbitals being filled (each orbital holds two electrons).
Not true: A, C and E.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.text: The large difference between the melting and boiling points of oxygen and sulphur may be explained on the basis of
questions.sol:
Oxygen exists as small $\mathrm{O_2}$ molecules, while sulphur exists as $\mathrm{S_8}$ rings. The much larger $\mathrm{S_8}$ molecules have far stronger van der Waals forces, so sulphur has much higher melting and boiling points.
The difference is explained by atomicity.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Which of the following ions is the strongest oxidizing agent?
(Atomic Number of Ce = 58, Eu = 63, Tb = 65, Lu = 71)
questions.sol:
The stable lanthanoid state is +3. $\mathrm{Tb^{4+}}$ ($4f^7$) readily gains an electron to become $\mathrm{Tb^{3+}}$, so it is a strong oxidising agent.
$\mathrm{Eu^{2+}}$ is a reducing agent; $\mathrm{Ce^{3+}}$ and $\mathrm{Lu^{3+}}$ are already in the stable +3 state.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Preparation of potassium permanganate from $\mathrm{MnO_2}$ involves two step process in which the 1st step is a reaction with KOH and $\mathrm{KNO_3}$ to produce
questions.sol:
Fusing $\mathrm{MnO_2}$ with KOH and an oxidising agent such as $\mathrm{KNO_3}$ gives dark green potassium manganate, $\mathrm{K_2MnO_4}$.
In the second step the manganate is oxidised (or disproportionates) to $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: One mole of the octahedral complex compound $\mathrm{Co(NH_3)_5Cl_3}$ gives 3 moles of ions on dissolution in water. One mole of the same complex reacts with excess of $\mathrm{AgNO_3}$ solution to yield two moles of $\mathrm{AgCl(s)}$. The structure of the complex is:
questions.sol:
Two moles of AgCl means two ionisable chlorides outside the coordination sphere; three ions in solution means one complex cation and two $\mathrm{Cl^-}$.
An octahedral cobalt needs six ligands: 5 NH$_3$ and 1 Cl.
$\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_5Cl]Cl_2}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements I and II.
Statement I: Dumas method is used for estimation of "Nitrogen" in an organic compound.
Statement II: Dumas method involves the formation of ammonium sulphate by heating the organic compound with conc $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Statement I is true: the Dumas method estimates nitrogen.
Statement II is false: in the Dumas method the compound is heated with CuO and the nitrogen gas is collected; forming ammonium sulphate with conc. $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ is the Kjeldahl method.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.text: Which one of the carbocations from the following is most stable?
questions.sol:
All four are allylic cations; the group on the far end of the double bond decides the extra stabilisation.
$-\mathrm{OCH_3}$ donates its lone pair through the conjugated system ($+R$), spreading the charge onto oxygen. This is the strongest effect.
In $-\mathrm{OCOCH_3}$ the oxygen lone pair is partly drawn into the C=O group, so it donates less. $-\mathrm{F}$ donates weakly ($+R$) against a strong $-I$. $-\mathrm{CH_2OCH_3}$ is not conjugated and only withdraws by $-I$.
The methoxy-substituted cation (2) is the most stable.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.text:
Following are the four molecules "P", "Q", "R" and "S".
Which one among the four molecules will react with $\mathrm{H{-}Br(aq)}$ at the fastest rate?
questions.sol:
Addition of HBr starts with protonation of the C=C bond to give a carbocation; the more stable the cation, the faster the reaction.
In Q the double bond carries the ring oxygen (an enol ether). Protonation gives a cation next to oxygen, stabilised by its lone pair (an oxocarbenium ion), which is far more stable than the tertiary cations from R and S or the secondary cation from P.
Q reacts fastest.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The conversion proceeds well in the less polar medium .
$\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-CH_2-Cl\xrightarrow{HO^-}CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-CH_2-OH+Cl^{(-)}}$
Statement II: The conversion proceeds well in the more polar medium .
$\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-CH_2-Cl\xrightarrow{R_3\ddot{N}}CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-CH_2-\overset{(+)}{N}R_3\ Cl^{(-)}}$
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Both are $S_N2$ reactions of a primary halide.
I: the reactants include a charged nucleophile ($\mathrm{HO^-}$) whose charge is spread out in the transition state; a polar solvent stabilises the reactant ion more than the transition state, so a less polar medium favours the reaction. True.
II: neutral reactants ($\mathrm{R_3N}$ and RCl) form a charge-separated transition state and ionic products; a more polar medium stabilises these and speeds the reaction. True.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Aman has been asked to synthesise the molecule (x). He thought of preparing the molecule using an aldol condensation reaction. He found a few cyclic alkenes in his laboratory. He thought of performing ozonolysis reaction on alkene to produce a dicarbonyl compound followed by aldol reaction to prepare "x". Predict the suitable alkene that can lead to the formation of "x".
questions.sol:
x is 1-acetylcyclopentene. Ozonolysis of 1-methylcyclohexene (1) cuts the ring C=C bond to give $\mathrm{CH_3CO(CH_2)_4CHO}$ (6-oxoheptanal).
An intramolecular aldol condensation then follows: the enolate from the $\mathrm{CH_3CO}$ side's $\alpha$-$\mathrm{CH_2}$ attacks the aldehyde carbon, closing a five-membered ring. Dehydration gives the conjugated enone, 1-acetylcyclopentene.
So the alkene is 1-methylcyclohexene.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Which of the following arrangements with respect to their reactivity in nucleophilic addition reaction is correct?
questions.sol:
Ketones are less reactive than aldehydes (more steric hindrance and two electron-donating groups), so acetophenone is least reactive.
Among the aldehydes, an electron-donating $p$-$\mathrm{CH_3}$ lowers the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon and an electron-withdrawing $p$-$\mathrm{NO_2}$ raises it.
acetophenone < p-tolualdehyde < benzaldehyde < p-nitrobenzaldehyde.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The product (A) formed in the following reaction sequence is
questions.sol:
i) $\mathrm{Hg^{2+}/H_2SO_4}$ hydrates propyne (Markovnikov) to propanone, $\mathrm{CH_3COCH_3}$.
ii) HCN adds to give the cyanohydrin $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2C(OH)CN}$.
iii) $\mathrm{H_2/Ni}$ reduces $-\mathrm{C\equiv N}$ to $-\mathrm{CH_2NH_2}$: A is $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2C(OH)CH_2NH_2}$, option (2).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
The carbohydrate "Ribose" present in DNA, is
A. A pentose sugar
B. present in pyranose from
C. in "D" configuration
D. a reducing sugar, when free
E. in $\alpha$-anomeric form
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.note: Kept as printed: the question says ribose is present in DNA; the sugar of DNA is 2-deoxyribose (ribose is in RNA). The statements tested hold for both sugars, and the answer follows NTA's final key.
questions.sol:
The sugar of nucleic acids is a pentose (A), of the D-series (C), and as a free sugar it reduces Fehling's/Tollens' reagents (D).
In nucleic acids it is present as a furanose ring (B false), in the $\beta$-form (E false).
Correct: A, C and D.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Consider the following reaction occurring in the blast furnace:
$\mathrm{Fe_3O_4(s)+4CO(g)\rightarrow3Fe(l)+4CO_2(g)}$
'$x$' kg of iron is produced when $2.32\times10^3$ kg $\mathrm{Fe_3O_4}$ and $2.8\times10^2$ kg CO are brought together in the furnace. The value of '$x$' is _____. (nearest integer)
{Given:
molar mass of $\mathrm{Fe_3O_4}=232$ g mol$^{-1}$
molar mass of CO $=28$ g mol$^{-1}$
molar mass of Fe $=56$ g mol$^{-1}$}
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{Fe_3O_4}$: $\dfrac{2.32\times10^6}{232}=10^4$ mol. CO: $\dfrac{2.8\times10^5}{28}=10^4$ mol.
$10^4$ mol $\mathrm{Fe_3O_4}$ would need $4\times10^4$ mol CO, so CO is limiting.
Fe $=\dfrac34\times10^4=7500$ mol $=7500\times56$ g $=420$ kg.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Standard entropies of $\mathrm{X_2}$, $\mathrm{Y_2}$ and $\mathrm{XY_5}$ are 70, 50 and 110 J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$ respectively. The temperature in Kelvin at which the reaction
$\mathrm{\dfrac12X_2+\dfrac52Y_2\rightleftharpoons XY_5}$ $\quad\Delta H^\ominus=-35$ kJ mol$^{-1}$
will be at equilibrium is _____ (Nearest integer)
questions.sol:
$\Delta S^\ominus=110-\dfrac12(70)-\dfrac52(50)=110-35-125=-50$ J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$.
At equilibrium $\Delta G^\ominus=0$: $T=\dfrac{\Delta H^\ominus}{\Delta S^\ominus}=\dfrac{-35000}{-50}=700$ K.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
37.8 g $\mathrm{N_2O_5}$ was taken in a 1 L reaction vessel and allowed to undergo the following reaction at 500 K
$\mathrm{2N_2O_5(g)\rightleftharpoons2N_2O_4(g)+O_2(g)}$
The total pressure at equilibrium was found to be 18.65 bar.
Then, $K_p=$ _______ $\times10^{-2}$ [nearest integer]
Assume $\mathrm{N_2O_5}$ to behave ideally under these conditions.
Given: R = 0.082 bar L mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$
questions.sol:
$n=\dfrac{37.8}{108}=0.35$ mol, so the initial pressure is $p_0=0.35\times0.082\times500=14.35$ bar.
If $2p$ of $\mathrm{N_2O_5}$ reacts, the total is $p_0+p=18.65 \Rightarrow p=4.3$ bar.
$p_{\mathrm{N_2O_5}}=5.75$, $p_{\mathrm{N_2O_4}}=8.6$, $p_{\mathrm{O_2}}=4.3$ bar.
$K_p=\dfrac{(8.6)^2(4.3)}{(5.75)^2}=9.62=962\times10^{-2}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Xg of benzoic acid on reaction with aq $\mathrm{NaHCO_3}$ released $\mathrm{CO_2}$ that occupied 11.2 L volume at STP.
X is _____ g.
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{C_6H_5COOH+NaHCO_3\rightarrow C_6H_5COONa+H_2O+CO_2}$: 1 mol acid gives 1 mol $\mathrm{CO_2}$.
11.2 L at STP $=0.5$ mol, so 0.5 mol benzoic acid ($M=122$) $=61$ g.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Among the following cations, the number of cations which will give characteristic precipitate in their identification tests with $\mathrm{K_4[Fe(CN)_6]}$ is _____.
$\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}$, $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$, $\mathrm{Ba^{2+}}$, $\mathrm{Ca^{2+}}$, $\mathrm{NH_4^+}$, $\mathrm{Mg^{2+}}$, $\mathrm{Zn^{2+}}$
questions.sol:
Potassium ferrocyanide is the confirmatory reagent for:
$\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}$: chocolate-brown precipitate of $\mathrm{Cu_2[Fe(CN)_6]}$.
$\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$: Prussian blue, $\mathrm{Fe_4[Fe(CN)_6]_3}$.
$\mathrm{Zn^{2+}}$: bluish-white precipitate of $\mathrm{Zn_2[Fe(CN)_6]}$.
$\mathrm{Ba^{2+}}$, $\mathrm{Ca^{2+}}$, $\mathrm{NH_4^+}$ and $\mathrm{Mg^{2+}}$ are identified by other reagents. Number $=3$.
questions.subject: Chemistry
